cohort: 491,590 women and their children in New South Wales, Australia
finding: Children born by spontaneous vaginal birth had fewer short- and long-term health problems compared to those born after birth interventions.
mod_finding: Infants born by instrumental birth after induction or augmentation had the highest risk of jaundice compared to spontaneous vaginal birth, while children born by cesarean delivery were at increased risk for infections, eczema, and metabolic disorder.
